correctness.rationale: The coordinate lower bounds are true facets and force the unique reflexive translate center c=(1,...,1); any actual adjacent-sum facet of integral capacity b then has primitive lattice distance qb-2=1, so qb=3. For s>=2,d>=3, the first and second upper bounds are independent genuine facets of capacities s and s+1; their required indices conflict. For s=1 and odd d>=3 the first and final even-indexed facets have capacities 1 and 2, again conflicting. For s=1 and even d the even bounds are redundant and the polytope is a product of standard 2-simplices, reflexive after 3P-1; d=2 allows s=1 or3 only by qs=3. This proves necessity/sufficiency and minimal indices for every stated integer pair. Independent integer dilation/Ehrhart inversion confirmed 25 pairs d=2..6,s=1..5 including h*(d4,s3)=(1,90,284,94,1); this bounded check is not the infinite proof.
